text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday the housing cycle appeared to have passed its trough, but the recovery through 1997 would be gradual rather than a boom.
"Most would agree, certainly our assesment (is) that the cycle has bottomed and turned, but I wouldn't be predicting booms," Costello told reporters after the relase of December quarter GDP data.
"I think it will be a gradual recovery throughout the course of 1997, which is consistent with the views that we've putting of strengthening growth through 1997 and 1998."
Data released earlier on Tuesday showed average GDP rose 0.5 percent in the December quarter to be 3.1 percent higher over the year.

Data released on Tuesday showed a 10.4 percent rise in January building approvals, and economists said then while the strength was probably overstated, the outlook was for a firming housing sector through 1997.
